paragraphs: On Thursday, Coach Matt took the class to the ground for a ball match. Before the game, Leo made a score card with glue and colored paper. The card was full of small stars, one for each point. "Who is ready?" asked Coach Matt. Leo's team was the blue team, and Mia was in it too.

It was Leo's turn first. He took the bat in his hands and looked down at it. He swung hard, but the bat did not touch the ball. He swung again and missed again. The third time, the ball hit his foot, and the other team laughed a bit. Leo's face was hot, and he put the bat on the ground. He did not want to speak to anyone.

Coach Matt came and sat next to him. "Speak to me, Leo," he said. "What is the problem?" "I cannot hit the ball," said Leo quietly. "Good try," said Coach Matt with a smile. "You swing very fast, but you look at the bat." "Look at the ball, and not at the bat." "Turn your shoulders, and swing slowly." "Then try again."

Leo took the bat and stood up. Mia put her hand on his shoulder and said, "You can do it." Leo looked at the ball with both eyes. He turned his shoulders and swung slowly. The bat hit the ball, and it flew across the ground. "Run, Leo!" shouted Mia. Leo ran to the end of the line, and the blue team scored a point.

At the end of the match, the blue team had four points. The other team had five points, so the blue team lost. Leo did not mind. "I hit the ball," he told Lily after the lesson. He put a gold star on his score card. "Thank you, Coach Matt," he said. "Well done, Leo," said Coach Matt.
text.summary: Leo cannot hit the ball in the sports class and feels bad. Coach Matt gives him simple feedback, and Leo tries again and scores a point for his team.
